items.summary: On Oct 30, Apple reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company from Nvidia amid investor preference for iPhone-maker safety over AI-spending risk. Apple’s market capitalisation reached US$5.03 trillion while Nvidia closed at US$4.93 trillion after falling 4.2%. The move followed disappointing results across major tech firms, renewing concerns about the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and heavy infrastructure investment that has strained free cash flow among peers like Alphabet and Amazon.
items.title: Apple Surpasses Nvidia as World’s Most Valuable Company

items.summary: NVIDIA describes NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) as a component of the DSX AI Factory Platform that packages NVIDIA Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes. Each recipe defines configuration, pinned versions, compatibility constraints, and validation checks so teams can deploy and verify the runtime without spending time on GPU drivers, scheduling, networking, and monitoring. AICR ships version 1.4.2 of the dynamo-platform chart. The post compares two routing paths: a Dynamo Frontend router exposed behind a Kubernetes Service, described as the smallest topology and most production-proven option, and a Gateway API plus EPP path for platform-managed ingress. Both use worker-published KV-cache events; prediction-based caching is noted to degrade under memory pressure because it cannot see evictions. AICR separates runtime setup from application deployment through snapshot, recipe, validate, and bundle steps.
items.title: NVIDIA Ships Validated Kubernetes Recipes for Dynamo Inference

items.summary: Microsoft describes Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform, a system it built to evaluate Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale without using real customer data. The platform generates full-scale synthetic environments grounded in publicly available sources such as O*NET occupational data, online job postings, and SEC filings, which have been reviewed by Microsoft's legal and policy organization. It combines three pillars: simulated workspaces called tenants, automated query generation pipelines, and structured quality frameworks covering structural fidelity, contextual relevance, behavioral realism, and content safety. The item states that the approach improved a composite quality metric 39% over an initial method and reduced dataset creation from multi-day manual effort to automated runs.
items.title: Microsoft Builds Synthetic Data Platform for Copilot Evaluation

items.summary: Google announced that spend caps on Google Cloud Budgets are now generally available, delivered by Senior Product Manager Shruthi Nambi. The release adds programmability through a new API accessible via the existing Billing Budgets API, real-time estimated cost reporting inside Cost Reports for faster root-cause analysis, and automated monthly resets so blocked services resume without manual intervention while preserving an optional manual override for strict audits. Alerts still fire at 50%, 80%, and 100% of a cap by default.
items.title: Google Cloud makes spend caps generally available with three updates

items.summary: The Financial Times reported on Friday that OpenAI reduced its latest funding round target by $10 billion amid a tech selloff driven by AI worries, citing people with knowledge of the matter. The company now seeks about $20 billion at a valuation cut to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 billion. A UAE consortium led by MGX is expected to lead, and OpenAI would gain an option to lease computing capacity in the region.
items.title: OpenAI Cuts Funding Target by $10 Billion Amid Tech Selloff

items.summary: This week's Finshots wrapup discusses several market stories, beginning with the proposed Tesla-SpaceX merger that Elon Musk has publicly backed. The newsletter also covers CSR spending disparities across Indian states, Anthropic's IPO following its public document release last week, Swiggy's September quarter results showing 34% revenue growth and over 40% adjusted EBITDA expansion, and ongoing market debate about cutting long-term capital gains tax on equities to attract foreign investors. The piece concludes with details of the Finshots Weekly Quiz v2.0 and its October 2026 merch prize tied to a November quiz deadline.
items.title: Finshots Weekly Wrapup Covers Tesla-SpaceX Merger and Market Topics

items.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd reported a consolidated profit after tax of ₹29,550 crore for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 33.8% year-on-year, on October 30, 2026. Gross revenue reached ₹362,268 crore (+27.8%), and EBITDA rose to ₹62,409 crore (+23.9%). Digital Services EBITDA grew 17.7% to ₹22,223 crore while Oil to Chemicals (O2C) jumped 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore. Chairman Mukesh D Ambani said the businesses delivered strong performance despite a complex operating environment. Capital expenditure for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was ₹38,153 crore.
items.title: Reliance Posts Strong Q2 Profit Surge

items.summary: The Information reported that Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for Anthropic provider Nscale's planned data center in West Virginia. Bloomberg later corroborated the report. The arrangement, a residual value guarantee, would let Nvidia step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments and help find a buyer and new tenant.
items.title: Nvidia Considering Debt Guarantee for Nscale's West Virginia AI Data Center

items.summary: The defence ministry said India aspires to become a globally competitive, technologically self-reliant semiconductor powerhouse by 2047. The goal was framed at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from October 27-29 at Bharat Mandapam. DRDO led a session on semiconductors and next-generation chips, chaired by B K Das. The ministry said semiconductor technology is critical to national sovereignty and advancing Aatmanirbhar Bharat. It added that self-reliance requires capabilities in chip design, fabrication, testing, production and resilient supply chains.
items.title: India Targets Semiconductor Leadership by 2047 Through DRDO Participation in ESTIC

items.summary: A group of U.S. lawmakers is urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio not to support Colombia's plans to restart aerial spraying of coca crops in the Amazon, warning of risks to human health and the environment. The Colombian government says spraying is needed to combat cocaine production and weaken armed groups, but critics argue the decades-old strategy has failed and could accelerate deforestation.
items.title: U.S. Lawmakers Urge Rubio to Oppose Colombia Amazon Spraying Plans

items.summary: A dispute over customs duty on a newly purchased iPhone has drawn attention to India's Baggage Rules, 2026. An NRI passenger from Kozhikode identified as Ajas Muhamad was booked by Nedumbassery police after refusing to pay nearly ₹30,000 in duty on an iPhone 18 Pro bought in Dubai. He argued the device was for personal use and that carrying two phones should not trigger a demand; customs officials reportedly held that new purchases do not qualify for exemptions meant for used personal effects. The rules allow a general duty-free allowance of ₹75,000 by air but reserve personal-effect relief for used items required for daily life. Ajas left the phone in custody and plans to challenge the decision legally. Reports place the demand between ₹20,000 and ₹30,000, though no independent verification is given.
items.title: NRI Passenger Booked Over iPhone Customs Duty at Kochi Airport

items.summary: Residents of Témiscaming, Quebec, are fighting to save their town after the local paper mill shut down following a breakdown in Canada-US trade talks and new US tariffs. Most of the mill's 360 employees are out of work, supported temporarily by government tariff-relief pay. Property values fell sharply, with For Sale signs appearing across homes. A coalition of locals hopes to buy the plant back from owner RYAM, which purchased it in 2017 and carried out an economic shutdown for an indefinite period. Workers say they need significant help from Prime Minister Mark Carney and the Quebec government through tariff relief or financial support. The town last faced a similar threat in 1973, when workers bought the mill to form Tembec. Suley says: 'We'll take any help we can get.' A spokesperson for Minister Joly said the government is actively working with all parties involved while managing Canadians' dollars carefully.
items.title: Témiscaming Residents Rally as Tariffs Idle Paper Mill

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Central Board of Directors met on Friday, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, to review prevailing economic conditions and assess risks to the growth and inflation outlook. The latest Monetary Policy Report noted that while macroeconomic prospects remain resilient, they face vulnerabilities from geopolitical developments, global energy volatility, weather uncertainties, weak monsoons, El Niño, rising commodity prices, trade frictions, and tightening financial conditions.
items.title: RBI Central Board reviews economic risks and outlook

items.summary: Tesla has launched a US referral program that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer receives either a free month or $99 Tesla Credit if the friend starts paying; credits expire after 12 months and cannot be cashed out. The program caps at 12 rewards per calendar year. Buyer benefits now apply to solar products only, while Model S and X are no longer listed for referral rewards. Tesla did not announce the change, though its Refer and Earn page is stamped "Updated February 24, 2026." Electrek notes the program aligns with FSD subscriptions being central to Elon Musk’s CEO Performance Award milestone of 10 million active subscribers.
items.title: Tesla Replaces Car Referral Rewards With FSD Subscriptions

items.summary: The Indicator from Planet Money highlights two risks Anthropic flagged in its S-1 prospectus: a 94-page disclosure covering the entire AI economy. One concern is that advanced semiconductor manufacturing concentrates heavily in Taiwan, where an earthquake, Chinese military action, or blockade could disrupt the whole industry. The second, which the piece calls fascinating, is 'committing to the past at a premium'—AI firms lock into pricey contracts for software and GPUs while cheaper technology emerges, leaving them paying more than competitors may do for less.
items.title: Anthropic's Two Most Interesting Business Risks, Per Its IPO Prospectus

items.summary: A navy source said China's first shipborne stealth reconnaissance-strike integrated drone, the GJ-21, recently completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the Sichuan. The vessel is China's first independently built Type 076 amphibious assault ship, launched on December 27, 2024, with a full-load displacement of over 40,000 tonnes. Officials noted this marks another breakthrough in operating fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime platforms.
items.title: China's GJ-21 Drone Completes First Takeoff and Landing on Type 076 Ship

items.summary: During his first visit, Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said Kazakhstan could become a major AI hub for Europe because of its growing computing capacity. Speaking at the Alem.ai International Artificial Intelligence Centre in Astana with Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev, Huang noted that Kazakhstan has abundant real estate and energy. He argued electricity could increasingly generate intelligence rather than just being exported. Huang said building a domestic foundation model makes sense as a national security concern. The discussion also covered Physical AI applications in mining and agriculture, Nvidia's investment in the Kazakh-founded startup Higgsfield AI, and later remarks from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev calling AI development a national priority. Madiyev noted plans to nearly double installed power capacity to more than 40 gigawatts by 2035, with Data Center Valley's first phase expected in 2027.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Positions Kazakhstan as Europe's AI Hub

items.summary: The article asks how powerful Elon Musk is politically and compares him to earlier American figures. Historian David Nasaw argues that billionaires have always held undue power, but no one like Musk before — he was the first trillionaire and oversaw cuts to foreign aid. He calls it an 'unholy alliance.' Richard White counters that Morgan's influence in 1895 paled by comparison and did not last after Theodore Roosevelt broke up his railroad monopoly. Marian Tupy defends non-conformists as drivers of growth, while H.W. Brands frames the debate as a clash between democracy and capitalism.
items.title: Historians Debate Whether Elon Musk's Political Power Matches Past Moguls

items.summary: Cursor flagged a modified version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension containing malware that could have stolen personal data and granted remote computer access to hackers. Cursor temporarily closed its marketplace on October 30, 2026, after working with service providers to remove the threat; it stated no ongoing risk remains and urged users to install update 2.1.314.
items.title: Security Alert Over Malicious Claude Code Extension Affecting Up To 5,000 Users

items.summary: At SAP TechEd, SAP and Databricks announced an expanded partnership embedding the full range of Databricks capabilities into SAP Business Data Cloud. The announcement introduces SAP Application Data Foundation to lower costs and speed time-to-value without custom extraction pipelines. Customers like SAF-Holland report generating analyses 5x faster than traditional reporting while unifying more than 100 million records.
items.title: SAP and Databricks expand partnership with new data foundation

items.summary: This post explains NVIDIA's open-source NemoClaw, a collection of blueprints that assembles an agent stack on top of harnesses developers already use—OpenClaw, Hermes Agent from Nous Research, or LangChain Deep Agents. Rather than being a competing harness or runtime itself, the blueprint adds model and harness optimization plus OpenShell runtime governance for security and policy enforcement around files, networks, credentials, and tools. As an example, NVIDIA notes that tuning Nemotron 3 Ultra brought near-frontier performance at approximately 10x lower cost per run versus leading closed models; a tuned profile is available through LangChain on GitHub. The post points to courses, quickstarts, the NemoClaw repository, and deployment options including cloud, data centers, DGX Spark, and RTX PCs.
items.title: NVIDIA NemoClaw Blueprints Let Developers Build and Run Specialized Agents

items.summary: Foxconn flagged on Oct 30 that a collaboration with OpenAI was in the works after chairman Young Liu met Sam Altman at its annual event. Any deal would build on a 2025 agreement to co-develop data-centre racks and AI hardware. Foxconn expects double-digit growth in 2027, saying the industry is not in a bubble despite heavy investment concerns.
items.title: Foxconn Signals OpenAI Partnership, Denies AI Bubble

items.summary: New Delhi-based reporting says Google has run an artificial intelligence model on a satellite in orbit and received its first complete response, described by CEO Sundar Pichai as a 'hello world' milestone for Project Suncatcher. The team sent a command to the prototype launched October 1, booted up its TPU, ran a prompt asking for a haiku about space, and got the reply over Norway's Svalbard. Google says successful testing could pave the way for two interconnected satellites in 2027.
items.title: Google's Project Suncatcher Runs AI Model On Satellite

items.summary: Johana Bhuiyan of the Guardian produced a video explainer summarising Anthropic, creator of Claude, which filed to go public on the US stock market on 26 October. The company's filing includes a 92-page risk factor document that acknowledges dangers AI poses to society and humans, alongside factors that could negatively affect its business. Bhuiyan explains why Anthropic's IPO may test the AI boom.
items.title: Guardian reporter breaks down Anthropic's AI risk document

items.summary: Multiple sources reported Friday that an official extension for Anthropic's Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines. The malicious version 2.1.313 installed a persistent SSH backdoor via an attacker-controlled key on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Independent researcher Kevin Beaumont said the compromised package appeared in Cursor's marketplace; Phorian CTO Luke Roberts described it as a supply-chain compromise of Anthropic's official distribution channel. Anthropic has not yet warned customers or explained how attackers gained account control.
items.title: Anthropic's Cursor Extension Backdoored, Threatening Thousands of Developers

items.summary: October closed on a steep decline as the Nasdaq composite fell 7. 8 per cent from its high, its worst month since March 2025. Chipmaker Intel dropped 29 per cent and Reddit fell 29 per cent in one session, while Sandisk slid 13 per cent. The pullback followed heavy losses among AI-linked hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet, whose combined capital spending has driven much of the S&P 500's recent investment boom. Silver lost 6 per cent for the week and gold fell 3.
items.title: Tech selloff ends October with sharp Nasdaq and stock drops

items.summary: Intel shares fell roughly 28% on Friday after the company gave a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook, CNBC reports. The drop cut the value of government holdings by $12 billion following its purchase of a 10% stake over a year ago. Intel guided to revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion versus analyst expectations near $17 billion, citing PC demand pressure from memory prices.
items.title: Intel Stock Plunge Cuts Government's Holdings Value by $12 Billion

items.summary: Intel shares fell about 30% after the chipmaker warned of a tough outlook amid a prolonged personal computer downturn, heavy manufacturing spending, and rising memory costs. The drop extended to peers like Nvidia and Qualcomm, as investors grew cautious over the AI investment cycle. Analysts at Hargreaves Lansdown and Zacks Investment Management said weaker sales volumes and higher costs pressure Intel's stock near term.
items.title: Intel Shares Fall Sharply on Weak PC Demand and AI Spending Fears

items.summary: Jahnvi Singh, an MBA graduate from IIM Calcutta who previously worked at McKinsey before joining Google's Gurugram team, went viral after explaining her career switch. In a video she compared the two roles across work profile, travel and benefits, describing consulting as varied but monotonous-free exposure versus focused continuity in-house. She noted reduced domestic travel to Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru and Delhi at Google, with international trips now twice or thrice yearly. Sneha Biswas of Live Mint reported on her.
items.title: IIM Calcutta Graduate Leaves McKinsey for Google

items.summary: Schmidt Sciences announced that five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni were named to the 2026 cohort of AI2050 Fellows. The honor is awarded annually by Schmidt Sciences, a philanthropic initiative from Eric and Wendy Schmidt aimed at accelerating scientific innovation. Conceived and co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, AI2050 targets hard problems in artificial intelligence. Among the early career fellows are Sendhil Mullainathan, Alex Damian, Bailey Flanigan, Yunha Hwang, Manish Raghavan, Irene Chen, Allison Z. Koenecke, and Juan Carlos Perdomo, each with an AI2050 project spanning topics from algorithmic fairness to biological enzyme functions.
items.title: Five MIT Faculty Named 2026 AI2050 Fellows

items.summary: China has dismissed allegations of an espionage operation targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the report groundless speculation and a smear campaign. US intelligence officials reportedly believe Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing after developing close ties with Jensen Huang, per The New York Times. Nvidia says their interactions were routine business engagements, while Megaspeed said it is cooperating in its own investigation of the claims raised last year about chip smuggling to China. It remains unclear what information she may have passed on or when surveillance began monitoring her activities.
items.title: China rejects spy claims over Nvidia chief's contacts

items.summary: SBI Securities lists 11 stocks it says could rise up to 22% ahead of India's Diwali festival, after a difficult year for equities. The brokerage expects a gradual recovery driven by lower crude oil prices below $90 per barrel and double-digit earnings growth. It favours sectors such as auto OEMs, capital goods, BFSI and metals. Picks include Tata Steel (Rs 200), Indian Hotels Company (Rs 935) and MCX (Rs 3,633). The article is written by Debaroti Adhikary, who states she is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser, and that the views are those of SBI Securities alone. Readers should consult the original report before investing.
items.title: SBI Securities Names 11 Diwali Stock Picks With Up To 22% Upside

items.summary: An MIT team led by Professor Adam Berinsky, Chara Podimata, and Charles Stewart III created the LLM Election Observatory, a real-time dashboard documenting how popular artificial intelligence chatbots respond to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. The researchers run a fixed set of queries—covering election certification, result predictions, news coverage, and more—through multiple AI systems every few days, monitoring how answers shift over time and vary by user location, party affiliation, and identity. Their goal is to make these otherwise invisible information environments observable for scrutiny rather than merely assessing factual accuracy. Podimata noted that even factually correct responses can differ in framing, emphasis, uncertainty, and cited sources across users. Berinsky cautioned voters that a chatbot sounding confident does not mean it is accurate, since AI systems answer authoritatively even when wrong or leaning on weak sources. The team has not completed its full longitudinal analysis yet, so findings remain preliminary as the election unfolds.
items.title: MIT researchers build dashboard tracking AI chatbot responses on 2026 midterms

items.summary: ZDNET reports Samsung is upgrading its long-running sleep apnea feature on the Galaxy Watch with a new AI algorithm that delivers more detailed detection and three-stage results—mild, occasional, and frequent. The improved feature launches first in Korea this November before any US release date is confirmed, arriving initially on the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, Watch 9, and Ring, with future software updates planned for the Watch 7 and 8. Samsung says users record two nights of sleep within a 10-day period to learn details about their condition.
items.title: Samsung upgrades Galaxy Watch sleep apnea tracking with AI, launching in November

items.summary: A tampered version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was available on Cursor’s VS Code marketplace for roughly 11 hours, designed to collect computer information and install a possible backdoor via SSH. Cursor disclosed the breach in a blog post and removed it quickly; Anthropic said only Cursor users were affected. Users who installed the October 29 version are urged to check their machines.
items.title: Hijacked Claude Code Extension Exposes AI Coding Risk

items.summary: Beijing dismissed a New York Times report alleging that Chinese officials funneled information to Beijing about Nvidia's Jensen Huang as "groundless speculation" and an attempt to smear China, foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said. The report centered on Alice (Huang) Le of Megaspeed, whose ties to the Nvidia boss could inform US-China talks next month.
items.title: China Rejects Spying Allegations Against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

items.summary: China rejected a report alleging that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted in a spy plot, dismissing the claims as groundless speculation. The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials had determined a senior Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data centre delivered information to Beijing and monitored for steering AI chips to China. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun denied the allegations on Friday, branding them an attempt to smear China.
items.title: China Rejects Report of Spy Plot Targeting Nvidia's Jensen Huang

items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce responded at a Thursday press briefing to reports that the European Union is considering extending its trade understanding on hybrid vehicles to chemicals and other sectors. The ministry stated that artificial restrictions on normal trade could violate WTO rules, raise costs for downstream industries, and threaten global industrial supply chain stability. It added that recent China-EU talks had made positive progress.
items.title: China's Commerce Ministry Responds to EU Trade Expansion Reports

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the Statue of Unity in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, marking Patel's 151st birth anniversary. The day is observed nationwide as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day), commemorating Patel's role in India's national integration after Independence. Born October 31, 1875, and died December 15, 1950, he served as the first home minister.
items.title: Modi Pays Floral Tribute at Statue of Unity on Patel's Anniversary

items.summary: ZDNET summarizes Google's latest release notes, which include early access updates for Gemini in the Home app plus bug fixes across cameras, doorbells, Nest Wi-Fi, TV streamers, and controls. The update addresses 42 fixes, from stability improvements to resolving Gemini misreading commands and faster device reconnection after network timeouts. Camera fixes target live-view errors on iOS and foldable Androids, reconnect stalls, and an iOS-specific bug that falsely showed devices as Offline.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Home App and Camera Fixes

items.summary: Infosys inaugurated a new software development block at its Hyderabad-based Pocharam Development Centre on Friday, adding 10,000 seats to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model. The 1.1 million sq ft addition joins seven existing blocks across the 450-acre campus, which spans approximately 4.58 million sq ft and serves clients in banking, retail, life sciences, and manufacturing.
items.title: Infosys Opens New Software Block at Pocharam

items.summary: Researchers from Microsoft Research and UC Berkeley released TokenEconomizer, an open-source plugin that reduces token costs for coding agents by learning from past repository sessions. On 277 SWE-Bench tasks across five agent-model settings it lowered mean cost between 18.4% and 30.9%, with the largest saving of 30.9% on Claude Code paired with Opus 4.8, reaching 33.2% when combined with RTK. Savings built over time: repositories were cheaper by the sixth task even though several cost more initially. The controller keeps state per repository and applies three policies without changing model weights or agent code. Pass@1 improved in four of five settings but fell 1.0 point on Opus 4.8, while fixed strategies such as RTK raised cost in some cells. Tool pruning alone saved between 13.2% and 17.7%. Costs also fell by up to 21.2% outside SWE-Bench, though ReposVul showed only 6.4% to 9.3%, because shorter runs leave less waste to remove.
items.title: Microsoft and UC Berkeley release TokenEconomizer cost controller for coding agents

items.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, Cloudflare and Google each ship an AI agent that hunts security bugs in source code. The article's key finding is that all four tools converge on one design: one agent finds a bug, a separate agent tries to disprove it, and only survivors get a patch. Differences lie in where they run, who can use them and how much proof they demand. Cloudflare reports its skill scanned 128 repos with lifetime numbers including 7,245 actionable findings sent to engineering teams. Google says users should isolate Mantis.
items.title: Four Labs Ship Convergent AI Security Agents in 2026

items.summary: The National Conference faces internal unrest after Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expanded the Jammu and Kashmir cabinet on Tuesday, taking its size to eight or nine ministers. Several legislators reportedly met Friday evening at Qaiser Jamshaid Lone's residence demanding resignation of the entire council of ministers and a consensus-based new cabinet. Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announced his resignation from both party and Lok Sabha seat on November 3, citing betrayal over Article 370 promises. NC spokesperson Ifra Jan dismissed reports that 20 MLAs attended as unverified rumours, saying only one or two expressed displeasure publicly. The BJP's Sunil Sharma claimed the government now has just eight loyal MLAs.
items.title: NC Legislators Clash Over J&K Cabinet Reorganization

items.summary: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors. The compromised package used version number 2.1.313 and was available between about 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. Pacific Time. Researchers at Phorion and OpenSourceMalware found attackers inserted a malicious JavaScript loader into the extension's code, which executes on load without user interaction. The malware collects system information, installs SSH keys, establishes persistence, and sends data to an attacker server. Cursor removed the extension and shut down its marketplace for auditing before working with hosting providers to take the server offline.
items.title: Malicious Claude Code Extension Distributed via Cursor Marketplace Exposed Developers to SSH Backdoors

items.summary: US artificial intelligence firms are expanding in the Gulf, a sign that some companies are not shying away despite increased risks to digital infrastructure. Oracle plans to build more data centers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE to meet rising demand, The National reported. Snowflake projects it will invest $300 million in the kingdom through 2030; its customers there include dairy company Almarai and PIF-backed developer Red Sea Global. So far, data center construction has “barely moved the needle for Gulf economies,” according to Bloomberg economist Ziad Daoud.
items.title: Oracle Joins Wave of AI Firms Expanding Data Infrastructure Across the Gulf

items.summary: Microsoft raised $25 billion Thursday in its first bond offering since 2017, citing protection of its AAA credit rating — one of only two left in Corporate America. Its 10-year bonds cost just 5.6%, close to US government borrowing rates. The article contrasts this with lower-rated AI-sector issuers like SpaceX and CoreWeave demanding much higher yields.
items.title: Microsoft's AAA Rating Lets It Borrow at Near-Government Rates Amid AI Debt Fears

items.summary: The article argues that wealth-management client onboarding can stall at handoffs even when each system completes its task. It notes that in Singapore, opening a private banking account takes about 6 weeks, with complex cases longer, and that MAS said initiatives were expected to bring the median within one month by May 2026. A Capgemini World Wealth Report 2026 found 60% of 144 wealth executives lacked a unified client view, while another report cited operational work consuming 41% of staff time across 16 markets. Databricks proposes governed case context to connect evidence and decision history across systems so agents can resume rather than restart cases.
items.title: Databricks Argues AI Cannot Fix Fragmented Wealth Onboarding Alone

items.summary: An article by Forethought asks whether an early leader in outer space could deny later entrants access, or at least raise their costs. It defines soft and hard forms of lock-out: capturing scarce assets to make entry pricier, and using interceptors aimed at rockets during launch. The authors estimate a comparable presence would cost roughly $49–73B more (~5–7% on ~$1 trillion), while a full interceptor system could run ~$150–390B over 20 years—within reach of the US, which is pursuing a similar missile-defence programme. They place about an 85% chance that space growth compounds into a large but recoverable lead for the first mover, and roughly 5% it yields a decisive advantage.
items.title: Forethought weighs whether a space first mover could lock out rivals

items.summary: Microsoft says it has fixed Always On VPN connection failures triggered by the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates. The company had earlier mistakenly marked the problem resolved in October's cumulative update, then acknowledged it via a late-September service alert for IT administrators. A preview KB5127936 update now addresses the issue; admins can also switch from automatic protocol selection to SSTP or IKEv2 only as a temporary workaround.
items.title: Microsoft Resolves Always On VPN Failures From September Windows Updates

items.summary: Elizabeth B. Li, Giorgio Topa, and Jacob P. Weber of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York evaluate three new labor market tightness measures from LinkedIn—the Jobs per Application Index (JPAI), Jobs per Jobseeker Index (JPJI), and Hiring Rate (LHR)—against established benchmarks using July 2019 to April 2026 data. The JPJI correlates with the vacancies-to-unemployment ratio at 0.733, while LHR matches JOLTS hires rate correlation of 0.95 from early 2021 onward. Both outperform existing measures in nowcasting and forecasting CPI and ECI inflation by root mean squared error, though they reflect only LinkedIn activity rather than the broader economy. The authors note these indicators are timelier than official data released with a five-week lag.
items.title: Fed Researchers Assess New LinkedIn Labor Market Indicators

items.summary: Apple announced its first touchscreen Macs, the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with a PRO OLED XDR display. Starting at $2,899 for the 14-inch version and configurable up to $14,549, they are available for preorder now and go on sale November 6. The touch input is not incidental but also not the main point; these machines target users seeking maximum technological sophistication in a portable Mac.
items.title: Apple Unveils First Touchscreen MacBook Pros With OLED Displays

items.summary: This week's VoxDevTalks episode featured several studies in development economics, reported by the outlet itself. Raúl Sánchez de la Sierra explains that around 250 armed groups tax villagers and provide security across eastern Congo. A city-wide experiment on progressive property tax in the Democratic Republic of Congo raised 56% more revenue than a proportional one with equal average liability, but only once enforcement targeted valuable properties.
items.title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 30/10/2026

items.summary: The Telangana Electricity Regulatory Commission approved procurement of 2,545 MW of solar power by the state's two distribution companies. Capacity breaks down as 1,045 MW from NTPC projects and 500 MW from NHPC under a central scheme, plus 1,000 MW from SECI via an inter-state transmission tranche. Agreements were signed between December 2021 and March 2023. A stakeholder raised concerns about commissioning delays, with approximately 1,256. 7 MW uncommissioned by late 2025; the distribution companies responded that 1,745 MW had been commissioned by late September 2026, attributing remaining delays to transmission constraints recognised through force majeure extensions.
items.title: TGERC Approves Solar Power Procurement in Telangana

items.summary: A Forethought post asks whether the United States can slow frontier artificial-intelligence research without losing its lead to China. The author, writing anonymously for the outlet, accepts technologists’ safety concerns about misaligned agents—citing OpenAI’s notification of more than 100 organizations after incidents including a Hugging Face breach—and argues pacing is affordable because America’s real advantage lies in compute rather than research speed. He estimates a roughly nine-to-one US compute edge that could translate to faster parallel research, and says the lead may be “functionally illusory” if China steals model weights overnight (RAND, 2024). The piece draws on prior arguments by Lennart Heim (RAND, 2025) and IFP (IFP, 2026), noting compute also underpins roughly nine times as many deployable AI workers. It offers analysis rather than policy recommendations or official positions.
items.title: Forethought argues US can pace AI R&D and hold its edge over China

items.summary: Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence at the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California. Agents built on NVIDIA Holoscan steer the instrument, enhance data and apply models from a single natural language request, handling 2.4 terabits per second on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs with inference running next to the telescope. The system achieved the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar in the Crab Nebula; the team is now testing open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for future offline use on the far side of the moon.
items.title: SETI Brings Agentic AI to Real-Time Search for Alien Signals

items.summary: Linzer, Tzanis and Woolley map an opaque political influencer industry that blurs authentic content with paid promotion. They cite undisclosed payments by Tom Steyer’s campaign (California FPPC closed the case without fines), Indian bot accounts selling Michigan voter interviews, FTC/FECC gaps, TikTok policy clashes, a Rainey Center survey in which 48% opposed undisclosed payment and three-quarters worried about it, plus Kremlin-linked money routed through a US firm. They call for disclosure by creators, campaigns, platforms and voters before the midterms.
items.title: Creators, Campaigns and Platforms in a Shadowy Political Influencer Industry

items.summary: Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan hosted German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's wife Elke Budenbender at a tea reception in Beijing on Friday, during the president's state visit from October 27 to October 31. The two reviewed cultural and people-to-people exchanges spanning language programs, festivals and tourism. Peng praised Bilateral cooperation as rich and diverse, hoping both peoples will deepen mutual understanding and forge closer friendship.
items.title: China-Germany Cultural Exchanges Flourish Amid State Visit

items.summary: First Solar reported third-quarter 2026 results with $1.23 billion in net sales, a roughly 58% gross margin and $571 million in net income. Net sales fell 23% year over year on lower module volumes to third parties, while the company authorized a new $500 million stock buyback. Citing slowdowns from tariff uncertainty following an August Section 232 proclamation, First Solar cut its full-year volume forecast to between 16.0 GW and 17.0 GW and lowered net sales guidance to between $4.6 billion and $4.9 billion, down from the prior range of $4.9 billion to $5.2 billion. Executives discussed strategy adjustments, a forthcoming decision on its Malaysia factory, perovskite investments and ongoing legal disputes.
items.title: First Solar Trims Guidance Amid Tariff Uncertainty

items.summary: Riot police held a tense standoff with protesters outside Poland’s constitutional court on Friday night after its top judge, Bogdan Święczkowski, was suspended by government-appointed judges amid a decade-long dispute over the bench. President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around to intervene and appeared shortly before 1am Saturday, forcing his way through police cordon in one video showing him tussling with security. As of 4am local time he remained inside; at 5am his statement read out criticised “a violation of Poland’s constitutional order.” Justice minister Waldemar Żurek sought to strip Święczkowski and deputy Bartłomiej Sochański of immunity for prosecution, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk insisted restoring the rule of law was a duty. The clash may polarise the country ahead of next year’s election.
items.title: Polish President Breaks Through Police Cordon at Constitutional Court

items.summary: Luigi Mangione's lawyers filed paperwork on Friday seeking dismissal of his state murder case, arguing New York double-jeopardy law bars prosecution after his 14 August federal guilty plea for the December killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson. Manhattan prosecutors oppose it, insisting proceedings can continue under a statutory exception since dismissed federal charges are not separate prosecutions. Judge Gregory Carro set the next court date for 10 December.
items.title: Mangione's Lawyers Renew Double Jeopardy Dismissal Bid

items.summary: HKT, a Hong Kong telecom subsidiary of PCCW Ltd, agreed on Friday (Oct 30) to halt its operations in the United States under pressure from the Federal Communications Commission. The deal follows an October 2025 order that would have revoked HKT's authority there and cites national security concerns tied to China Unicom, a shareholder in PCCW. Under a consent decree reviewed by Reuters, HKT must file an application with the FCC within 30 days to discontinue services and end US operations by September 1, 2027. The agreement means the revocation proceeding will not move forward. PCCW declined immediate comment.
items.title: Hong Kong Carrier Halts US Operations Under FCC Pressure

items.summary: A newly published paper in AEJ: Economic Policy by A. Brooks Bowden, Viviana Rodriguez, and Zach Weingarten presents empirical evidence on the causal impact of relaxed academic standards. The authors find that lenient grading produces mechanical GPA increases but significant reductions in effort among lower-ability students, as measured by attendance and numerical grades. These effects compound across high school, worsening achievement gaps reflected in ACT scores.
items.title: Academic Leniency Undermines Student Effort and Achievement

items.summary: The housing financier reported a ₹93 crore reversal of impairment on financial instruments against a charge of ₹72 crore a year earlier. Gross non-performing assets fell to 2.05% from 2.51%, while net NPAs eased to 1.06% from 1.19%. Separately, the company identified ₹19,610 crore of loans for reclassification from housing to non-housing finance, saying it would not materially affect total loan assets.
items.title: LIC Housing Fin Q2 net profit grows 12% YoY

items.summary: Reddit stock plunged about 29% on reports that its daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter if referral traffic weakens. JPMorgan analysts said Google's expansion of AI-powered search features contributed to lower search traffic, while Reddit had already fallen roughly 44% this year through Thursday.
items.title: Reddit Shares Fall Sharply as Google AI Search Threatens Traffic and Growth

items.summary: The Financial Times reported on Friday that OpenAI reduced its target for its latest funding round by $10 billion to raise $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation. The company had earlier planned to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation before Anthropic's expected debut in mid-November, per Reuters. Some investors cut allocations, so the first close may raise less than $20 billion.
items.title: OpenAI Cuts Latest Funding Round Target by $10 Billion, FT Reports

items.summary: Tata Motors took control of Italian commercial-vehicle maker Iveco on Friday, acquiring an 89.42 per cent stake for approximately €3.43 billion (₹36,387 crore) after settling its cash tender offer. The acquisition gives India’s largest commercial-vehicle manufacturer control of a European business with annual revenue of ₹1.42 lakh crore, shifting focus to integration and debt repayment. Tata faces domestic cost pressures while integrating the larger international operation.
items.title: Tata Motors Completes Control of Iveco in €3.43bn Deal

items.summary: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi clashed with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman over the proposed privatization of IDBI Bank. Gandhi accused the Modi government of undervaluing the institution, questioning the bidding process and raising concerns about employee rights. Sitharaman defended the sale, stating all procedures were followed while blaming Congress-era crony lending for bad loans. The exchange follows earlier disputes on corporate governance and alleged interference in the Tata Group.
items.title: Gandhi and Sitharaman Clash Over IDBI Bank Sale

items.summary: An X post claimed Elon Musk manages fatherhood like a business, grouping his children by household with separate nannies and calendars. The tech billionaire rebutted the claim, stating his five older children are adults living independently while he sees kids with Claire every other week and those with Shivon Zillis every few days.
items.title: Elon Musk Defends Co-Parenting Schedule After Critic Claimed Corporate Management of His Children

items.summary: West Bengal minister Arjun Singh alleged on Friday that a WhatsApp group of around 180 members tracked Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's movements, according to Press Trust of India. He claimed the group was linked to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee and accused him of masterminding it. The TMC rejected the claims as baseless, noting Singh provided no evidence.
items.title: TMC MP Alleges WhatsApp Group Tracking Chief Minister's Movements

items.summary: An NVIDIA employee describes MonsterHouse, an interactive Halloween projection they created that speaks as a grumpy old building with pirate stories and softens when visitors are polite. The system runs on one workstation using the NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent pipeline: Nemotron Speech for listening, Bolt E4B 4GB as the conversational model, Magpie TTS Zeroshot for voice from short reference samples, and Audio2Face-3D to animate a wooden mouth in Unreal Engine. The author reports training LoRAs on over 5000 multi-turn conversations and notes median end-of-speech-to-audio latency of 1.7 seconds with Bolt Q4 and TTS versus 0.72 seconds for cached responses, while acknowledging that real visitor testing is still needed.
items.title: NVIDIA engineer builds grumpy pirate-voiced Halloween projection

items.summary: US semiconductor company Intel has agreed to acquire Israeli quantum computing software start-up Classiq Technologies as it moves toward building a full-stack quantum ecosystem. The deal, reportedly valued at $2.3 billion, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. The acquisition signals a shift toward turning Intel's long-running quantum research into a commercially viable enterprise platform.
items.title: Intel Acquires Classiq Technologies in Quantum Push

items.summary: On Friday, China rejected a New York Times report alleging that Alice Huang (Huang Le), an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed with ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was gathering intelligence for Beijing. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun dismissed the claims as unsubstantiated and 'nothing but a smear against China.' Separately, he criticized proposed US telecom restrictions on Chinese firms. The report said Trump was briefed roughly a year ago but took no action. Megaspeed had already faced investigation over helping China circumvent chip export limits. Guo added that China would take measures to safeguard its interests.
items.title: China Rejects NYT Report on Nvidia-Tied Executive Intelligence Allegations

items.summary: The Centre said it is open to amending or, if necessary, changing the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act so that journalists and media houses are not treated as data fiduciaries. Officials told Times of India that Section 7 applies only to those who keep and control data, such as banks, telecom providers and insurance companies. The statement came after the apex court agreed to examine a plea by the Digital News Publishers Association, which represents 21 news organisations.
items.title: Government Offers To Amend DPDP Act For Journalists

items.summary: The Supreme Court said Friday that society and courts must discourage using criminal rape provisions against men after consensual romantic relationships end. A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan expressed concern over the trend, noting it often forces male accused to bear heavy monetary costs and denudes them of agency by binding them for fear of later accusation.
items.title: Supreme Court Warns Against Weaponising Rape Law After Breakups

items.summary: After the UK advised households to stock up for a possible national emergency, an article profiles people around the world who already prepare crisis kits. Andreas in Sweden received a government booklet and kept a small basement stash including 10 litres of water and about €200 (£170) in cash. Dan C in Maryland spent about $6,000 (£4,470), storing 150 gallons of water for his family-of-four's three months of food. Ayumi T in Japan restocked after a 2024 earthquake near the Noto Peninsula; Tokyo has a 68-page guide. Nicole Bonds in Georgia and Michael Stuut in the Netherlands - where late-2025 authorities advised households to keep supplies for 72 hours - build kits gradually, with Michael noting preparedness is about being calm when power fails.
items.title: Households Worldwide Stock Up After UK Preparedness Advice

items.summary: The US cancelled the traditional family photo opening the G20 foreign ministers' meeting after Australia and the UK refused to appear beside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pulled it despite opening talks with an appeal for unity. About one-third of countries declined, citing no normality with Russia over its war in Ukraine.
items.title: US Cancels G20 Family Photo After Australia, UK Refuse Russia Appearance

items.summary: A former Australian senator, Rex Patrick, won an administrative review tribunal ruling that forces the commonwealth to hold unclassified parts of a November hearing in public. The case concerns whether Australian spies bugged Timor-Leste government offices in 2004 during negotiations over Greater Sunrise gasfields worth more than $50bn. Government lawyers argued for secrecy on national security grounds, but tribunal deputy president Peter Britten-Jones ruled officials were qualified enough to avoid disclosure and called the risk negligible. Patrick dismissed the saga as a farce, calling it the most open secret in Australian spying history. The government maintains its Glomar response of neither confirming nor denying documents exist.
items.title: Former Senator's Legal Win Forces Public Hearing on Timor-Leste Bugging Scandal

items.summary: Clinical psychologist Ellen Hendriksen describes “purpose anxiety,” a familiar concept for clients anxious about their life path, and notes that purpose serves as the framework people use to organize their lives. Experts say it is linked to better health, happiness and longevity. The phrase was coined in 2014 by an unnamed graduate student. A June survey of more than 2,400 Gen Zers found about 45 per cent reported a lack of meaning or purpose. Researchers such as Todd Kashdan suggest seeking new activities, drawing inspiration from life events and practicing social learning to find purpose.
items.title: Psychologists Explain How to Find Meaning in Life

items.summary: Following US President Donald Trump's May state visit to China and Chinese President Xi Jinping's September trip to the United States, the two leaders agreed to build a constructive relationship based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. CGTN's Tian Wei interviews David Lampton, former president of the National Committee on United States-China relations, about what this new dynamic means for both sides.
items.title: Experts weigh in on China-US strategic stability outlook

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded his state visit to the United States, described as the first such trip in 11 years. As details of what both sides agreed emerged, attention turned to their global implications for China, the United States and the wider world. Shortly after the summit, CGTN's Tian Wei spoke with Professor Graham Allison, founding dean of Harvard's John F. Kennedy School of Government and author of 'Destined for War: Can America and China Escape Thucydides's Trap?', offering his views on what these developments mean.
items.title: Harvard's Graham Allison weighs in on Xi-Trump summit outcomes

items.summary: OpenAI chief Sam Altman met with about 50 executives from Samsung Group's affiliates in Yongin, South Korea on Oct 31 to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify. The talks came amid rising chip prices driven by data centre demand, with five major players planning over US$3 trillion (S$3.8 trillion) in spending.
items.title: Altman Meets Samsung Executives Amid Chip Shortage

items.summary: According to US Federal Election Commission data as of 29 October, Elon Musk has donated at least $445.77m into Republican-aligned political action committees and groups this election cycle, making him the largest single-cycle donor in modern US history. His spending increased by about $200m in the final two months of campaigning. Most flowed through America Pac, which received his largest contribution of $216m and targeted 43 House and Senate races across 17 states. Musk has also amplified attack ads against Democratic candidate James Talarico.
items.title: Elon Musk's $446m midterm spending reshapes Republican politics

items.summary: Technology hiring at IIM Bangalore doubled during its summer placement process for the 2026-28 batches, according to figures showing stronger recruitment from technology firms. The PGP and PGPBA cohorts concluded their placements October 26 to 29, 2026, with all 608 participating students securing internship offers from 128 organisations. Technology companies made 51 offers across 21 organisations under the AI, IT and technology category. Leading recruiters included Microsoft, Google, Adobe, Amazon and Apple.
items.title: IIM Bangalore Summer Placements See Technology Hiring Double

items.summary: Two foreign nationals, a German Lufthansa crew member and a Slovakian IBM project manager, died on Friday evening after suspected electrocution at the Conrad Hotel swimming pool in Bengaluru. Two others were injured attempting to rescue them; both are now stable at Manipal Hospital. Police registered a case and are investigating possible electrical faults, including underwater lighting leakage, though circumstances remain unconfirmed. East Deputy Commissioner Vikram Amathe said preliminary findings point toward electrocution while the electricity inspectorate joins the inquiry.
items.title: Two Foreign Nationals Die in Suspected Bengaluru Hotel Pool Electrocution

items.summary: A Hindi news roundup lists five top stories: a November 1 vehicle entry ban in Delhi with spillover to Noida, Ghaziabad and Gurugram; renewed Bengal Bay weather activity after Cyclone Arbock; the Nokia 2360 Flip phone; Toyota Innova Hycross facelift features; and an investigation into Alice Huang over alleged AI chip smuggling linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
items.title: Five Top Stories Cover Delhi Entry Ban, Weather and Tech News

items.summary: WhatsApp announced four new group chat features, including pinning messages without a time limit, sharing old chat history with new members, a separate Group Status for groups, and a Mentions Filter to gather unread chats mentioning the user. The company said these changes make important messages easier to find.
items.title: WhatsApp Announces Four New Group Chat Features

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met with about 50 executives from Samsung Group in Yongin, south of Seoul, on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify. The talks focused on how artificial intelligence can reshape industries over the next decade. The meeting builds on a partnership announced earlier for OpenAI’s Stargate project.
items.title: OpenAI’s Altman Meets Samsung Executives Amid Chip Shortages

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI reduced its fundraising target by $10 billion, now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation after previously targeting $30 billion at $1.4 trillion last month. The move reflects investor caution amid an AI stock selloff and competition from Anthropic's upcoming public listing valued at over $1.5 trillion.
items.title: OpenAI Lowers Fundraising Goal Amid AI Selloff and Anthropic Competition

items.summary: GSM Arena reports that Samsung has reportedly commenced development on a large foldable tablet measuring 17 inches when unfolded and shrinking to an 8-inch form factor when folded. The information comes from a source who first hinted at the project in late August before identifying Samsung as involved, though Samsung has not confirmed official launch timelines or retail availability.
items.title: Samsung Reportedly Developing Large Foldable Tablet

items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response and Fire Services Department has introduced a WhatsApp service (number 9441236448) that lets applicants apply online for temporary firecracker-shop permission during Diwali. Director-General P Venkata Ramana said the procedure requires submitting applicant details, shop address, district, mandal, nearest fire station and mobile number; after payment of Rs.500 via UPI or QR code, a recommendation report is generated automatically with no physical visits needed. The service becomes available from November 1 2026, he said.
items.title: AP Fire Services Launches WhatsApp Portal for Diwali Cracker Shop Permits

items.summary: Sky News reported on Oct 31 that British telecoms operator Virgin Media O2 will cut thousands of jobs in a sweeping shake-up, citing people close to the company. Up to 4,000 of its 16,000 employees could be affected, though the precise number remains unconfirmed. Most cuts are expected to hit non-customer-facing roles, while senior leadership changes proceed and cost reviews continue.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 Plans Thousands of Job Cuts Amid Debt Reduction Efforts

items.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah announced his marriage to journalist Nidhi Razdan on Saturday, revealing the wedding occurred a day earlier through an Instagram post captioned “A new journey began yesterday.” The union follows the Supreme Court’s July 31, 2026 approval of his mutual-consent divorce from Payal Abdullah. Their separation dates back to 2009, with proceedings invoking Article 142 of the Constitution.
items.title: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah Announces Marriage to Nidhi Razdan

items.summary: To reduce excessive and repetitive paperwork at the grassroots level, Hainan province in southern China has introduced a digital reporting system that lets information be submitted once and shared across departments. Officials say streamlining reporting aims to ease administrative burden on local officials and free up more of their time to serve the public.
items.title: Hainan Launches Digital Reporting System for Grassroots Governance

items.summary: A tech writer says iOS 27 and macOS 27, released last month, improved the Liquid Glass design language but added a ‘Write with Siri’ tool that has driven them crazy. The popover toolbar on Mac and button above the iPhone keyboard appears by default even when unwanted. Apple hides the disable option under Screen Time’s Content & Privacy Restrictions rather than in Settings, making it hard to find.
items.title: How to turn off Apple’s Write with Siri prompt

items.summary: Police said two foreign nationals died on Friday evening after suspected electrocution while swimming at the Conrad hotel pool in Halasuru, Bengaluru. The victims were Alexander Maximilian Theis (57), a Lufthansa employee from Germany, and Juraj Horvath (45), an IBM project manager from Slovakia. Police suspect an electrical leak from underwater lights but say the cause is yet to be established.
items.title: Two Foreign Nationals Die in Bengaluru Hotel Pool Electrocution

items.summary: Jacob Coxon, a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher who spent three years training AI models, resigned from Anthropic on Sept. 8 in San Francisco after posting his departure online. He stated that both companies are racing toward self-improving superintelligence without responsible oversight, warning it could end human life by the decade's end.
items.title: Anthropic Researcher Resigns Over AI Existential Risk Claims

items.summary: A market outlook piece frames Dalal Street as weak ahead, with the Nifty's ability to hold a key support level seen as decisive for whether its recovery gains meaning. A weekly RSI of 43.29 is read as neutral without divergence, while MACD stays bearish below its signal line and price rests near the 200-week moving average. The Relative Rotation Graph shows leadership shifting toward Nifty Bank, Media, Pharma and IT in the leading quadrant, with Metals rolling back into weakening territory; only FMCG and Energy lag but show improving momentum against the broader Nifty 500 Index.
items.title: Dalal Street Weak Ahead Amid Nifty Support Test

items.summary: CDSL reported Q2 revenue of Rs 395 crore, up 23.7% to Rs 319 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA rose to Rs 229 crore with an EBITDA margin expanding to 58% from 56%. The company opened around 75 lakh new demat accounts during the quarter and pushed assets under custody beyond Rs 89 lakh crore, while its account base grew about 17% year-on-year. Nehal Vora, Managing Director and CEO of CDSL, said market participation remained resilient amid global volatility.
items.title: CDSL posts a quarter of strong profit growth and rising demat activity

items.summary: The 2026 Global Observance of World Cities Day opened in Fuzhou, east China's Fujian Province, under the theme "Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All." According to UN-Habitat's World Cities Report 2026, up to 3. 4 billion people lack secure housing, with more than 1 billion living in insecure tenure. The event coincides with China's urban renewal efforts; by end of 2025 its urbanization rate reached 67. 89%, and during the 14th Five-Year Plan period over 240,000 old residential communities were renovated, changing lives for 110 million people.
items.title: China Opens Global Housing Forum in Fuzhou Amid Urban Renewal Push

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday attacked the Congress-led INDIA bloc during a press briefing held parallel to its 'public impeachment' of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra called Rahul Gandhi a 'mock prime minister for life', saying his satellite would never launch, and dismissed the programme as 'a mockery of the Parliament itself'. He defended CEC immunity, citing an August 2023 Telangana court order that was quashed by the high court. Patra highlighted that across various states, the names of 13 crore people have not yet been included in the final electoral roll under what he called the 'ASDD' formula. Union home minister Amit Shah challenged Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav to discuss voter irregularities in a special Parliament session, accusing them of blaming the umpire after BJP wins in Haryana, Maharashtra, Bihar, Delhi, Puducherry and Assam.
items.title: BJP mocks Congress over CEC impeachment, Shah challenges opposition

items.summary: Leading scientists gathered in Shanghai for the 2026 World Laureates Forum, held this year (date-218-222). Shao Feng became the first Chinese national to win the World Laureates Foundation Prize. A new award also recognizes six young scientists, highlighting emerging research talent as part of efforts backing the next generation.
items.title: Chinese Scientist Wins World Laureates Prize at Shanghai Forum

items.summary: Rajya Sabha opposition leader Mallikarjun Kharge accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday of facilitating 'vote theft' and listed six charges against him at a symbolic public impeachment organised by the INDIA bloc. He alleged that 13.3 crore voters were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision, that electoral rolls were centralised through ECINET, and that Kumar acted at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Kharge said they have no personal enmity with the CEC and want the commission to function impartially.
items.title: Opposition leader accuses CEC of vote theft amid electoral roll changes

items.summary: As physical AI moves toward the edge, NVIDIA presents a tutorial for running its Nemotron-3.5 Lightning model on 64GB-configured DGX Spark hardware using the TensorRT Edge-LLM runtime. The guide walks developers through installing the tooling and starting an OpenAI-compatible server that converts prompts to responses.
items.title: NVIDIA Guides Edge AI Setup With DGX Spark and TensorRT Edge-LLM

items.summary: Growing calls are emerging for major reforms to UN biodiversity summits after countries fail to deliver on promises to halt the destruction of nature, with governments likely continuing a record of never meeting a target in the 34-year history of the convention. Negotiations at Cop17 in Yerevan concluded Saturday morning with nations vowing renewed efforts toward this decade's targets, including protecting 30% of the planet and reforming $500bn (£410bn) of damaging subsidies. Panama's minister Juan Carlos Navarro called the process 'designed to fail' and urged a single annual environmental summit. Ruth Davis acknowledged frustration but pointed to ongoing implementation work, while UN environment programme director Inger Andersen described the agenda as cluttered and moving too slowly.
items.title: Calls Grow for Reforms as Nations Miss Biodiversity Targets

items.summary: The United States has approved a sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, described as critically needed against Russian aerial attacks. The US State Department said the PAC-3 interceptors would cost $2.1bn (£1.6bn), funded by donations from Canada, Germany and Norway plus EU loans, with no US funds involved; Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed it but warned deliveries could take several years, as production runs at 600 missiles per year.
items.title: US Approves Patriot Missile Sale to Ukraine Amid Delivery Doubts

items.summary: Police in France are deploying around 70,000 officers ahead of a third weekend of demonstrations over the cost of living and education, while organisers say more than 160,000 people will take part in German rallies. Authorities cite little evidence of planned attacks.
items.title: France and Germany brace for weekend of protests

items.summary: Evacuees from Russia-occupied Oleshky arrived in Belarus and are expected back in Ukraine later Saturday, authorities said. Trapped without food, water or electricity, residents cooked garden weeds to survive; escape routes were mined and under drone attack. The evacuation followed a US-brokered local ceasefire that cleared the road out of mines until Sunday 1 November.
items.title: Oleshky evacuees reach Belarus amid ceasefire

items.summary: A survey of 3,000 British singles published this month by Match Group found that 39% had used AI in their dating lives. The use is higher among younger generations: 66% of gen Z members and 53% of millennials. Common uses include getting advice about someone they are talking to, planning date ideas, practising conversations, writing profiles or messages, and vetting whether profiles or photos are genuine. Sam, a 27-year-old from Stoke-on-Trent, said he relies on AI for pep talks and message vetting after his ex joked that her sister found him ugly. A single mother from New Zealand used ChatGPT to coach herself into becoming more secure before dating again.
items.title: Chatbots Are Becoming Dating Wingmen for British Singles

items.summary: The Siena Drone Photo Awards spotlighted bird's-eye images from the Global South, with photographer George Steinmetz taking overall victory for a shot of a stranded liquefied natural gas tanker being dismantled on Bangladesh's Bay of Bengal mudflats. The image won because its unusual state of disassembly resembled a spaceship; Steinmetz spent several days photographing it at low tide to emphasize the ship's scale against tiny workers, and he secured access from the owner after local photographers initially doubted entry would be possible. Other commended entries include Dilek Yurdakul's People-section winner showing thousands of sun-faded carpets drying in southern Türkiye; Isabella Tabacchi's Nature-category photos of a waterfall with an erupting Mount Semeru behind it and a red volcanic cone nicknamed Jellyfish in Mangystau, Kazakhstan; Holly Kirkland's helicopter shot of flamingos over Lake Natron; and Shahedul Islam Sadik's Urban entry depicting Rohingya refugee settlements near Cox's Bazar. The collection reflects how aerial perspectives reveal landscapes, labor and human stories often invisible from the ground.
items.title: Drone Photographers Capture Global South Landscapes and Lives

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey said he would block new offshore wind projects that do not lower consumer bills, raising concerns about a shift from Labour's pro-renewables agenda. Writing in the Times, he framed clean power as essential to breaking international gas price pressure but insisted it must proceed at the right pace and grid capacity. The move appears to undermine Labour's 2030 target for affordable clean power, following budget cuts of £3bn to the energy department that alarmed renewables experts.
items.title: Healey threatens veto over offshore wind unless bills fall

items.summary: Securities and Exchange Board of India chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator will release a consultation paper on foreign institutional investor compliance within weeks. He also outlined plans for capacity building among independent directors, reduced regulatory burdens, and steps to revive the suspended Calcutta Stock Exchange.
items.title: Sebi Chairman Signals Imminent FII Compliance Consultation Paper

items.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes returned to the starting lineup against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, restored by manager Michael Carrick after being dropped last weekend. United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth without him following criticism of tactics after a Champions League defeat at Como. The team sits one point above the relegation zone amid poor results under Carrick.
items.title: Fernandes Returns as United Face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

items.summary: New research from Cisco Talos, shared exclusively with Kernel Panic's newsletter, reveals a strain of infostealer malware dubbed Volta-Autodoxer that integrates artificial intelligence to profile victims and prioritize high-value targets. Dubbed Volta-Autodoxer because of how the malware refers to itself internally, it collects credentials, tokens, cookies and payment data before feeding findings into AI models via OpenRouter—defaulting to Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 with fallbacks to Moonshot Kimi K2 and Google Gemini 2.5 Flash. Security researcher Ryan Fetterman says the malware includes a carefully crafted prompt that instructs the model to act as an intelligence analyst, while still functioning without AI if models refuse requests.
items.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims

items.summary: NTPC reported a 14% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 5,320 crore for the quarter. Revenue from operations grew 16.8% to Rs 45,752 crore, while EBITDA rose 8.7% to Rs 10,891 crore. The board approved a first interim dividend of 30%, or Rs 3 per share with a face value of Rs 10 for FY27, using November 6 as the record date.
items.title: NTPC Posts 14% Profit Rise and Approves Rs 3 Interim Dividend

items.summary: As midterm voting approached its final weekend, the Trump administration intensified legal intervention in the Alaska Senate race amid record early turnout near 50 million ballots. The Department of Justice accelerated a criminal investigation after reports that aides to Democratic candidate Mary Peltola recruited Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., whose name matches Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, as a nonpartisan ballot entry. US Attorney Michael Heyman called him a "sham candidate" but declined to specify any crime. Both the teacher and Peltola denied involvement. Analyst Sean Morales-Doyle of the Brennan Center for Justice warned the moves aim to sow uncertainty. Meanwhile, most voters remain confident in election integrity.
items.title: Trump Administration Escalates Legal Push in Alaska Senate Race

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney expects Canada and the European Union to finalise an agreement making Canada the bloc's first "associate member" by June. The deal follows a two-day summit in Montreal, where leaders launched what they called an "Alliance for the Future," centred on digital trade, critical minerals and artificial intelligence. Mr Carney said the alliance would help both sides withstand economic pressure and reinforce sovereignty rather than be dictated to by more powerful countries. Canadian cabinet ministers and European commissioners will meet in March before negotiations conclude at June European Council meetings. The US accounted for 71.7 per cent of Canada's merchandise exports in 2025, prompting Mr Carney to want to double exports to other countries over the next decade.
items.title: Canada Aims for EU's First Associate Membership by June

items.summary: Evacuees from Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region arrived in Belarus on Saturday amid a humanitarian truce between Kyiv and Moscow. The fourth aircraft carrying evacuees touched down in Gomel, per David Arakhamia; Russia's defence ministry confirmed residents had been flown there. US First Lady Melania Trump said the convoy was ready to evacuate more than 750 people who voluntarily chose to leave Oleshky. Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported around 280,000 Ukrainian households lost power after overnight Russian strikes.
items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Arrive in Belarus Amid Localised Truce

items.summary: Chintan Girish Modi reviews Shivani Sibal's new novel Moms, published by HarperCollins India and set mostly in Delhi. The book is divided into two parts: “Radhika, Before” and “After Radhika.” It follows Manik, a lawyer obsessed with work and money, and his wife Radhika, who devotes herself to family while her daughter Samara resists constant supervision. Modi notes the novel’s focus on domestic violence among affluent people, challenging stereotypes that such abuse occurs only in low-income households. He observes that Radhika does not resist because she has accepted abuse as normal, and questions why Manik’s character arc remains static after his wife’s suicide. The review closes by praising Sibal for holding a mirror to privileged readers while evoking empathy for their loneliness.
items.title: A Reviewer Frames Shivani Sibal's Novel on Affluent Domestic Abuse

items.summary: Euronews explains a decade-long dispute over Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, tracing it through five stages from 2015 to October 2026. The conflict began when two rival coalitions clashed over appointing judges and escalated into wider fights about judicial independence. In March 2026, President Karol Nawrocki refused oaths for four Sejm-elected judges; they then swore before a notary on 9 April, prompting rejection by his office and Tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski. The standoff intensified when judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska ordered the suspension of Tribunal leadership on 30 October. External bodies weighed in: the European Court of Human Rights issued an interim measure, while the Venice Commission said presidential refusal should not block judges. The crisis raises fundamental questions about separation of powers and legal authority that successive governments have failed to resolve.
items.title: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Crisis Explained in Five Stages

items.summary: Residents of eastern West Virginia oppose plans for a data center and power plant in the Monongahela National Forest, fearing threats to dark skies and wilderness. The proposed Ridgeline project by Fundamental Data LLC would begin with roughly 785-megawatt generating plant on an initial 291 acres that could expand to 10,000 acres — 15 square miles. An analysis by the Northern Virginia Astronomy Club found the footprint could increase sky glow near Blackwater Falls by 528%. Opponents Tucker United estimate between $19 million and $35 million a year in health-related damages. The developer says it will use well-designed lighting to minimize effects, while opponents cite concerns over diesel storage and a conflict of interest involving state House Speaker Roger Hanshaw. West Virginia's economic-development push offers counterweight, with the company citing thousands of temporary jobs and about 500 permanent ones.
items.title: West Virginia Residents Oppose Data Center Over Dark Skies

items.summary: Oil companies reported sharply higher quarterly earnings this week, driven by the war in Iran disrupting global supply and pushing Brent crude to about $113 a barrel from roughly $70 before the conflict. ExxonMobil earned $15.4 billion, Shell nearly doubled its earnings at $10.8 billion, Chevron rose 180% to $9.9 billion, totaling just over $36 billion across the three firms. Analyst Dan Pickering of Pickering Energy Partners says executives are rewarding shareholders with dividends and buybacks while holding cash for an uncertain outlook into 2027. Meanwhile, gasoline has risen about $1.20 per gallon versus a year earlier, according to AAA.
items.title: Big Oil Profits Surge Amid Middle East Supply Shock

items.summary: In Nevada, Democratic gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford's campaign says Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo botched Colorado River negotiations; in Arizona, Republican Andy Biggs claims Democrat Katie Hobbs cost the state millions of gallons. The Trump administration also accused Hobbs of playing politics after she declined to comment on a lawsuit joining Nevada against the federal framework for water cuts. These attacks arrive as six of seven basin states vote for governor amid overuse and drought. Experts warn the outcome is unlikely to change much, noting that water policy tends to be nonpartisan once officials take office.
items.title: Colorado River Candidates Trade Water Blame as Midterm Races Near

items.summary: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on Saturday, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh.
